turns.user: My cover started on 20 May 2026. I've a consultant appointment on 17 November, so I'll be out of the waiting period by then, won't I?
turns.reply: If your cover began on 20 May 2026, 17 November 2026 is day 181, so it’s still within the waiting period. Cover starts on day 182, which is 18 November 2026; treatment from then is subject to the usual limits. Please check your cover start date in the member portal.

[04_waiting_periods#2]
Waiting periods. How the days are counted. The date your cover began is day 0, so the waiting period is days 0 to 181 and cover starts on day 182, which is 182 days after your cover began. turns.user: And if the 17 November appointment was for a knee injury from a fall?
turns.reply: The plan’s accident exception removes the waiting period, but I can’t confirm from this alone whether your fall qualifies. Ask the provider to state on the receipt that the treatment followed an accident; if only your own note says so, a claims assessor will review it. A consultant visit also needs a GP referral and is subject to the usual limits.
